title: Readiness and Resilience: The National Effort We Can't Delay
gist: RAND Europe researchers Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans argue that Russian sabotage attacks in Europe nearly tripled in 2024 and kept rising in 2025, and that European national resilience now depends less on raw defense spending than on whole-of-society frameworks binding government, industry, and civilians, with Nordic, Baltic, and Central European states far ahead of Western Europe in building such frameworks.

insights.claim: The number of Russian state-sponsored sabotage acts across Europe continued to increase in 2025 after nearly tripling in 2024 compared with prior years, with 34 documented Russian attacks in Europe in 2024, many linked to the invasion of Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: A near-tripling of state-sponsored sabotage year-on-year is a concrete escalation metric for pricing European infrastructure, defense-contractor, and insurance risk.
insights.quote: The number of Russian state-sponsored acts of sabotage across Europe continued to increase in 2025 after almost tripling in 2024 compared to preceding years.
insights.locator: Europe is already confronted on its own soil

insights.claim: Companies supplying arms to Ukraine — including BAE Systems, Rheinmetall, the German Diehl Group, and EMCO — have been targeted by sabotage attacks in recent years.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Names specific defense contractors under direct sabotage risk, relevant to security due diligence and insurance pricing for defense-sector investors and supply chains.
insights.locator: several companies supplying arms to Ukraine

insights.claim: Over a quarter of documented Russian sabotage attacks in Europe have been directed at the transport sector, the largest single-sector share, targeting perceived weaknesses in societal structures, industry, infrastructure, and government and military premises.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Identifies transport infrastructure as the leading sabotage target sector in Europe, a specific risk factor for logistics, rail, and port operators and their insurers.
insights.locator: The largest proportion of attacks however

insights.claim: Russian and Belarusian actors have weaponized hybrid pressures such as irregular migration against European states in the past, alongside physical sabotage.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Flags migration weaponization as a recurring, non-military hybrid-threat vector that border and frontline states must budget resilience planning for.

insights.claim: The authors argue that national preparedness must be founded on a whole-of-society approach spanning cyber security, supply chains, and societal cohesion to meet, contain, and deny hybrid and non-linear threats.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Sets out the core policy framework investors and policymakers should use to evaluate a European state's resilience readiness — not military spending alone but cross-sector coordination.
insights.quote: National preparedness must be founded on a whole-of-society approach to meet, contain and deny new threats.
insights.locator: It is increasingly apparent that European nations

insights.claim: Real increases in defense spending matter, but the authors contend it is the frameworks governing how such spending is deployed, not the sheer size of the budget, that will determine whether a nation's crisis response succeeds.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: A direct challenge to the common investor heuristic of using defense-budget growth alone as a resilience proxy — implementation frameworks matter more, a nuance relevant to European defense-sector analysis.
insights.quote: Although real increases in defence spending matter, it is the frameworks in place governing the deployment of such spending, rather than the sheer size of the budget, that will make or break a nation's response to crisis.
insights.locator: Although real increases in defence spending matter

insights.claim: European defense spending continues to rise year-on-year, but its overall preparedness impact is being undermined by the absence of comprehensive frameworks addressing the diversifying nature of threats.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Suggests continued European defense budget growth may not translate proportionally into actual resilience gains without parallel institutional reform — a caveat for defense-spending-driven investment theses.
insights.locator: European spending on defence continues to rise

insights.claim: The private sector — energy providers, food retailers, the transport industry, and their supply chains — holds critical physical and digital infrastructure and a skilled workforce needed for wartime economic mobilization, and governments that proactively engage industry help businesses plan for personnel and resilience.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Positions private industry — especially energy, food, and transport firms — as a direct stakeholder and partner in national resilience planning, implying government contracting and public-private partnership opportunities in these sectors.
insights.locator: The private sector has a critical role

insights.claim: Since Russia's invasion began, Ukraine's public and private sectors have jointly repaired telecommunications and critical infrastructure networks, exemplifying close government-industry-military collaboration under wartime conditions.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Offers a live wartime case study of public-private infrastructure resilience that other European states are being urged to emulate ahead of, not during, a crisis.
insights.locator: Close collaboration between the government, military

insights.claim: A rapid Ukrainian government relocation scheme launched in March 2022 supported 745 enterprises in moving their operations to western Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete, replicable precedent (745 relocated enterprises) for how European governments could plan industrial continuity schemes in advance of conflict.
insights.locator: a rapid government relocation scheme launched in March 2022

insights.claim: France has established an industrial reserve — a standing pool of former defence-industry staff available for mobilization during a national crisis — as a model for maintaining a registry of key wartime-production occupations.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Highlights a concrete French policy mechanism (defense-industry labor reserve) that other European states could adopt to reduce mobilization delay in a crisis.
insights.locator: France's recent efforts to establish an industrial reserve

insights.claim: Preparedness is far more embedded in national consciousness in Central Europe, the Nordics, and the Baltics than in Western Europe, with Finland, Sweden, Norway, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, and Germany actively strengthening resilience across society, government, and industry and building more advanced crisis-response frameworks.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Names the specific states leading European resilience-building, a useful map for identifying which national markets and defense-adjacent sectors are furthest along an institutional readiness curve.
insights.locator: In Central Europe, the Nordics, and the Baltics

insights.claim: The Nordic concept of 'Total Defence' is proposed by the authors as a blueprint that Western European leaders should adapt to their own national contexts to build comparable whole-of-society resilience.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Flags 'Total Defence' as the reference model likely to shape upcoming Western European resilience legislation and defense-policy design.
insights.quote: The Nordic concept of "Total Defence" serves as a blueprint for Western European leaders to translate into their own context.
insights.locator: All of this must be underpinned

insights.claim: The authors argue achieving continent-wide resilience will require difficult conversations across European NATO on security and preparedness, including mechanisms that mandate, incentivize, and where needed compensate civilian participation in preparedness.
insights.speaker: Lucia Retter and Judith Huismans
insights.so_what: Signals coming policy debate and potential new compensation/incentive legislation for civilian participation in national resilience across NATO's European members.
insights.locator: A Europe capable of deterring, denying and defeating
